comments: Thanks for reporting this! We currently don't have full support for many features of the `Array` dtype, but that's on my todo-list. :)

review_comments: In the case of the `DateTime` type, before this change, we got an `ArrayChunked` with `UInt64` inner dtype instead of `DateTime`.
Ah, yes. We store the physical arrays, but the dtype must keep the logical type. :+1:

I feel like I've found the culprit :). It seems we only consider the `validity` array in `push_null`. But unlike `LargeListArray`, there is no `offsets` array for `FixedSizeListArray`, causing our `values` to be confused with `null` value. After changing this, the test passed.
Ah.. yes. It hurts that we need to box that every time, but that's what it is. :(

Without this change, `Array` construction would still not actually from `any_values_to_array`. It actually constructs a `list` and then converts it into an `Array`.

It seems this change broken tests. But I have a feeling this has nothing to do with the PR.

Failed case:

```python
    payload = [[1, 2, 3], None, [4, 2, 3]]
    dtype = pl.Array(pl.Int64, 3)
    s = pl.Series(payload, dtype=dtype)
    assert s.to_list() == payload
```

```python
Expected :[[1, 2, 3], None, [4, 2, 3]]
Actual   :[None, [4, 2, 3]]
```

@ritchie46, I'm not sure if this related to #12817. But as for the same reason, the changes in that PR are not actually covered by tests.

I have added a `debug(out.len)` before `line 195`, it somehow print `out.len() = 2`  instead of `3`. 🤔 

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/7b1c8d5098b843a3be2abd209697a60d23223205/crates/polars-core/src/series/any_value.rs#L194-L199
Alright, I manage to only pick the change of `fn new_array()` to the `main` branch, so that we can directly construct `Array` from any values. This test case still failed, seems unrelated to this PR.
I can take a look at the failing test?

Thanks! 🙇
